objective: 持续优化 EmbodiedForge 七个实际小时，保留已有工作区改动并提供可审查证据。
scope: CPU motion input loading/validation and NumPy object-conditioned sampling; shared unpinned host. Weave's upstream Torch sampler, simulation, GPU performance and training throughput were not measured.
verification_qualification: One earlier final-source subclass probe failed a combined input fingerprint check after 115660 completed cases. Its original record did not capture changed bytes or separate the constructors. The failure remains unclassified unless the explicit diagnostic says otherwise. Subsequent successful replays and restarted probes do not erase it or establish an uninterrupted failure-free seven-hour run.

historical_subclass_diagnostic.interpretation: Unclassified single fingerprint mismatch after 115660 completed cases in an earlier final-source subclass cohort. The original combined check saved neither per-field bytes nor before/after digests and cannot attribute a change to either constructor. Immediate exact replays and a 2001-case stage-separated byte diagnostic (1000 repetitions of the failing index plus its surrounding 1001 indices, 12006 stage checks) did not reproduce it. Two injected recorder controls passed. The original failure/log/source and the first successful diagnostic with a source-identifier metadata error are preserved. A restarted instrumented probe records its own coverage and duration. No source defect or harness defect is inferred; later passes do not erase the observed failure.

changes: Large exact ndarray fields validate in frame blocks targeting 262144 input scalars. Float16 quaternion norms, small fields and ndarray subclasses retain whole-field behavior to preserve computational tolerance/dispatch semantics. A frame wider than the target is processed whole; this is not a byte cap or file streaming.
Exact ndarray contact labels use equality membership, fixing NumPy 1.24 uint64 signed-table IndexError for ordinary arrays and NPZ-decoded inputs. Array subclasses retain existing isin dispatch.

Multiple requested objects share one per-call library scan and compact signed integer candidate buffers. Candidate order, RNG call order, output order, errors and later public object-list edits are preserved. Single-object calls retain the existing scan.
tradeoffs: Multi-object candidate grouping may need additional transient memory. The 65536-clip/64-object/128-request cases used about 0.56-0.57 MB instead of 0.08-0.10 MB. All raw signed memory and timing results are retained.
Whole-file loading remains dominated by NPZ decoding; small inputs can be flat or slightly slower. Selected synthetic reference-API gains do not establish training speedups.
Readonly byte fingerprints and weak-reference release checks run per case. File descriptor/thread/RSS checks are periodic observations, not general leak proofs or process memory limits.
